recommended.label: Tool change: Vacuum area frame > Suction cup > Nut runner

tools.display_name: Vacuum area frame, 2 x 3 cups, 600 mm
tools.rating: rated 8.47 kg on a smooth face (holding force over a 1.5 safety factor)
tools.caveat: Vacuum area frame (approximation): the cups of the suction cup model on a rigid frame, each with its own seal test and its own vacuum valve (a cup that does not seal stays off). The holding force is the sum of the sealed cups' caps; the payload is that force over a safety factor (1.5 smooth, 2.0 porous, 2.5 swivelling, all [assumed]) at 1 g. Only the smooth rating is a simulated claim: the porous and swivelling ratings are arithmetic on the same force, because no leak, porosity or swivel is simulated. Not modelled: a shared vacuum source and its flow, the leak of an unsealed cup into the others, the frame's flex, peel across a long face, foam or needle area grippers. Treat frame results as a screen, then verify on hardware.

Suction cup (approximation): a compliant lip of rigid segments on a bellows spring with a limited tilt; the seal is a geometric test (every lip segment touching the face, part material under 13 rays inside the lip) gating a MuJoCo adhesion actuator capped at vacuum x lip area (at most 60 kPa). The lip must touch the face: no pull across a gap. Not modelled: air flow, leak rate, porosity, vacuum build-up time (the vacuum follows the shared close ramp and is cut the control tick the seal is lost), lip material hysteresis, peel dynamics beyond the contact distribution. The lip's friction is the part's. Treat suction results as a screen, then verify on hardware.

tools.rating: rated 6.7 N m (clutch cap 10 N m); members at least 12 mm tall
tools.caveat: Nut runner (approximation): a rigid hex socket with a guide funnel on a lateral float; it engages a hex member by shape. The Studio wrist's roll is its spindle [assumed], at the wrist's speed: a clutch limits the torque to its cap (10 N m, under the wrist's 15 N m) and lets go at the release. The socket's walls are stacked slices so the simulator's contacts are as stiff as steel (a solver artifact). Supported in the Studio: members at least 12 mm tall. Not modelled: a motor, a torque transducer, cross-threading, socket wear, a reaction arm. Simulated, verify on hardware.

heroes.title: Floor tile setting
heroes.use_case: Floor tiling: a 300 x 300 mm porcelain floor tile (10 mm thick, 2.2 kg) goes on the fresh adhesive bed, where it sits about 2 mm proud of its finished height until it is pressed. Lay it on the bed, then tamp it down level: within 1 mm of its finished height and no more than 0.5 degrees out of level, pressing no harder than 60 N.
